newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ banks consider raising mortgage rates - sources.
newsitem.headline: NZ banks consider raising mortgage rates - sources.

text.p: New Zealand banks, squeezed by a sharp rise in short end money market rates over the last two weeks, are considering raising variable mortgage rates, bank sources said on Thursday.
"We are meeting today to discuss raising the rate or leaving it," a senior manager at a New Zealand bank said.
He asked not to be identified, but added he believed other banks were doing the same.
In the last week 90-day bank bill rates have surged above 7.5 percent in tandem with a slump in the New Zealand dollar.
Lenders have commented that recent cuts in retail variable mortgage rates will prove unsustainable if wholesale rates remain at current levels.

"You've got to look at rates and say it (raising mortgage rates) has got to be on the cards. I suspect everybody has got their finger on the trigger right now. We're just waiting for someone else to blink," an official from another bank said.
Banks' variable mortgage lending rates currently range between 8.25 percent and 8.95 percent.
The 90-day bank bill rate is currently at 7.72 percent.
